steps.note: Open the single-stage event creation flow.
Set the event to an auction using the price-based strategy.
Provide the required event title.
Apply the first offered auction template; the case does not provide an exact template name.
Add the requested product with quantity 10.
Enter the requested plant/location in the first line item's delivery-location cell.
Complete the auction pricing sheet after adding the line item.
Invite three QA vendors for the A, B, and C participant scenario without inventing vendor names.
Commit a 30-minute schedule starting now.
Publish the configured auction.
Confirm the event reached a published project page.
Submit Vendor A's initial bid.
Confirm the first vendor bid was accepted.
Submit Vendor B's lower bid.
Confirm the second vendor bid was accepted.
Return to the buyer console to inspect the buyer-side response view.
Open the buyer's Responses view for the auction.
Confirm that two direct vendor responses are visible to the buyer.
Assert that the buyer's response view exposes the best-price indicator.
Assert that the buyer can see the current best price of 95.
Open the available QA vendor supplier-portal session for vendor-side inspection.
Open the event's pricing round in the supplier portal.
Assert that the available vendor session can see the current best price of 95.
Submit a lower revision to exercise the valid-below-best-price bid behavior.
Return to the buyer console after the vendor revision.
Reopen the buyer's Responses view after the revised bid.
Assert that the buyer-side view reflects the new best price.
